chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, regarding
the man who mortgages with the man a mortgage, so something hits it or it is lost. He said: He returns his wealth to him (complete).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mortgaged item is lost or damaged while in the possession of the mortgagee?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Hammad ibn al-Halabi, this hadith establishes the principle of 'ghurm bi al-ghurm' (liability accompanies ownership/possession) in mortgage transactions. It clarifies that if the collateral is lost or damaged while in the mortgagee's custody, the debt remains due, and the mortgagee must compensate the mortgagor, ensuring the creditor's right is preserved despite the loss of the specific asset.
